title: Figure style test — crisp vs hand-drawn
date: Scratch
author: Shashwat Pandey

---

*Scratch page for picking a figure style. Two figures, each drawn both ways. The
hand-drawn versions are generated by a script (roughjs, the same library
Excalidraw uses) so they are inline SVG with no image assets and no GUI step.*

<figcaption>The naive kernel's fatal flaw. The warp wants 32 floats; because they sit in 32 different rows, the hardware moves 1024 bytes to deliver 128.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figcaption>Load 8 values of A and 8 of B into registers, then do every pairwise product: 16 loads buy 64 multiply-adds.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Crisp (what Part 1 ships today)** — see section 6 of
[Part 1](blog.html?post=cuda_gemm) for the shipped version of this one.

## Notes

The hand-drawn figures use the site's validated palette rather than Excalidraw's
defaults: blue and orange as the two real hues, plus a neutral. Green is
deliberately absent — paired with orange it measured &#916;E 7.0 under
deuteranopia, which is exactly the red/green trap, and in these figures those
colors mean "fast" and "slow".

The hand font falls back through Virgil, Excalifont, Architects Daughter and
Comic Sans. If none are installed the text renders in the default cursive face,
which is the one thing that would need a webfont to fix properly.
